governanceNotes: D1 batch 67 (2026-09-26): identity deferred (severity-continuum identity duplication plus no-identity outcomes plus zero condition-specific quantification). Osteopenia is a bone-mineral-density grade (T-score between -1 and -2.5) on the same DXA measure that defines osteoporosis, and the located evidence supports no outgoing catalog edge: (i) osteoporosis - the apparent progression relationship is a grade transition along one continuous measure (identity-duplication guard, consistent with the batch-66 optic-atrophy to blindness withhold), and the published osteoporosis window receives etiologic causes (hypogonadism, Cushing's, malnutrition, and eight others), not grade-progressions; (ii) fragility fractures - vertebral compression, hip, and other low-trauma fractures are the genuine clinical consequences of low bone mass but have NO catalog identities (withheld propositions, not deferred identities; the retraction watch note stands - the post-stroke osteopenia anchor PMID 17895057 was RETRACTED and remains excluded per the batch-59/60 ledger record); (iii) stress fractures - the catalog holds a stress-fractures identity but zero located quantification of stress-fracture risk in osteopenia specifically (the athlete low-energy-availability literature runs through hypogonadism and disordered-eating windows that own their own edges, ME-29); (iv) osteoarthritis - the located subchondral-bone literature runs osteoarthritis to subchondral bone loss, the reverse direction (direction-inversion guard). Reopening conditions: (a) a cohort quantifying incident osteoporosis or a catalog-fit fracture outcome in osteopenia with baseline BMD and treatment adjustment under a governance decision that treats grade-progression as registrable; or (b) addition of fragility-fracture identities to the catalog, which would unlock the preserved fracture-risk literature at once.
